questions.question: What is CRUD and how does ActiveRecord do it?
questions.title: ActiveRecord CRUD Basics
questions.direct_answer: CRUD is the four data operations — Create, Read, Update, Delete — that every app does on records. ActiveRecord maps them to model methods: Create (Model.create or new+save), Read (find, where, all), Update (update, save after changes), Delete (destroy). Each returns a model instance or a relation and runs the SQL for you. CRUD is the vocabulary of data apps, and ActiveRecord makes it a few method calls instead of SQL.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can name the four CRUD operations and the ActiveRecord methods for each (create/save/find/where/update/destroy).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using delete instead of destroy (delete skips callbacks), or not saving after new.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: CRUD = Create/Read/Update/Delete; ActiveRecord maps them to create+save, find/where, update, destroy. destroy (not delete) runs callbacks.

sections.title: The Four Data Operations
sections.content: CRUD is the four data operations every app does on records: Create, Read, Update, Delete. ActiveRecord maps them to model methods. Create: Model.create(attrs) builds and saves in one step, or m = Model.new(attrs); m.save. Read: Model.find(id), Model.where(...), Model.all. Update: m.update(attrs) or change attributes and save. Delete: m.destroy. Each returns a model instance or a relation and runs the SQL for you. CRUD is the vocabulary of data apps, and ActiveRecord makes it a few method calls instead of hand-written SQL.

sections.title: The CRUD Cycle
sections.content:
Create, read, update, delete — the four operations on records.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Create: new+save / create] --> R[Read: find/where/all]
  R --> U[Update: update / save]
  U --> D[Delete: destroy]
```

sections.title: CRUD with ActiveRecord
sections.content:
```ruby
# CREATE
user = User.create(name: 'Ada', age: 36)   # build + save in one step
#   or: user = User.new(...); user.save

# READ
user = User.find(42)                # by primary key
users = User.where(active: true)    # filtered relation

# UPDATE
user.update(age: 37)               # set attributes + save
#   or: user.age = 37; user.save

# DELETE
user.destroy                       # deletes the row AND runs callbacks
#   user.delete would skip callbacks (use destroy)
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using delete instead of destroy — delete skips model callbacks (and validations).
Calling Model.new and forgetting to save (the record isn't persisted).
Confusing update (saves) with assigning attributes (doesn't save until you call save).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: CRUD = Create, Read, Update, Delete — the four data operations.
Create: Model.create (build+save) or Model.new then save.
Update: update(attrs) saves; or set attributes and call save.
Delete: use destroy (runs callbacks), not delete (skips them).

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: CRUD is the four data operations every app does on records — Create, Read, Update, and Delete. ActiveRecord maps them to model methods. Create is Model.create of attrs, which builds and saves in one step, or Model.new then save. Read is find of id, where, or all. Update is update of attrs, which sets and saves, or you change attributes and call save. Delete is destroy. Each runs the SQL for you. CRUD is the vocabulary of data apps, and ActiveRecord makes it a few method calls instead of hand-written SQL. A common mistake is using delete instead of destroy, because delete skips model callbacks and validations, and calling Model.new and forgetting to save, because the record isn't persisted.
